rationale: Retain Summit Carbon Solutions under Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund III while removing TPG from the qualifying infrastructure-owner roster because its investment came from TPG Rise Climate, a climate-private-equity strategy rather than TPG's infrastructure mandate. Correct the platform to an active but unbuilt IA-NE-WY development after its 2026 reroute, without treating subordinate project entities or stale five-state scale as current operating assets.

companyFieldUpdates.description: Summit Carbon Solutions is developing a carbon-dioxide capture, transportation and permanent-sequestration network for ethanol producers in the Midwest. The company is an active development-stage infrastructure platform, but no construction start, full project-finance close or revised commercial-operation date was identified through August 19, 2026. After a 2026 reroute, the current core is focused on Iowa, Nebraska and Wyoming and retains 27 Iowa ethanol plants while removing approximately 200 route miles; the former approximately 2,000-mile, five-state and 20-million-ton annual design should not be treated as the current approved or operating footprint. Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund III invested in 2021 and remains the qualifying infrastructure owner. TPG Rise Climate contributed $300 million to the 2022 equity raise through a climate-private-equity strategy and is therefore not counted as a qualifying infrastructure-fund owner. Project, pipeline, capture, storage and site LLCs remain subordinate to the single Summit platform.
